caveats: Trained on a bounded recent-date sample (docs/project-status.md § Phase 3 detail), not the full ~19M-row dataset — do not generalize these numbers beyond this sample.
is_fraud is a SYNTHETIC dataset-generated label (docs/data-lineage.md § 5), not a real bank's ground truth.

Class imbalance is severe (see split.positive_counts above) — small absolute counts of positives in val/test make these metrics high-variance; treat point estimates cautiously, especially at the test-set scale.

Both models perform near chance (ROC-AUC ~0.46-0.50) on this sample. The dataset's own (excluded, diagnostic-only) fraud_score field DOES separate the classes clearly (see diagnostic_fraud_score_separation_by_is_fraud above) — so a real underlying signal exists in the generator's process, but it is not exposed through the transactional/behavioral columns this phase loaded. Leading hypothesis: the signal lives in device/session/IP data (digital_events -> Device derivation, Phase 5), which this ingestion run deliberately skipped for memory reasons (src/ingestion/README.md). This is reported as a real finding, not tuned away — see docs/implementation-roadmap.md Phase 4's own anticipated risk.

Structural proxies computed instead, below.
business_metrics.structural_proxies_MEASURED: see baseline_comparison's per-approach 'automation_rate' (share of cases resolved without a human) as an unpriced stand-in for 'human agent cost avoided' — not a dollar figure

sample.note: Every in-window fraud transaction plus a random sample of legitimate ones — an intentional oversample of the rare positive class for evaluation, not the dataset's natural ~0.09% prevalence (docs/evaluation-plan.md § 1).

policy_engine_override_rate.definition: share of cases where the mock LLM's own recommendation needed no human approval, but the Policy Engine's independent, fact-derived action-risk classification required it anyway (docs/decision-policy.md § 2, Scenario D) — the actual value the Policy Engine adds over 'LLM only', not visible in the flagged/precision/recall numbers above because those only track WHICH action was proposed, and the Policy Engine never changes that, only who may authorize it.

baseline_comparison.note: '4_hybrid_current_implementation' is Evidence Engine + Policy Engine + mock LLM + Human + the trained Fraud ML model's score (src/ml/score.py, Phase 15, docs/project-status.md § Phase 15 detail) — the fraud-score risk-escalation path docs/decision-policy.md § 5 always specified is now wired in, closing the gap this note used to flag. '3_llm_only' calls MockLLMClient directly, bypassing the Policy Engine (and the fraud-score override) entirely — deliberately unsafe in the way the hybrid design exists to avoid; measuring it is the point. MEASURED on this sample: rows 3 and 4 are STILL identical, and 'policy_engine_override_rate' did NOT change (still 19/152) — not because the wiring is inert, but because every fraud_model_score in this 152-case sample falls in a narrow band (~0.40-0.53) that never crosses either configured threshold (high=0.70, critical=0.90). This is a direct, measured consequence of the Phase 4 finding that this model performs near chance (test ROC-AUC~0.502) — its predicted probabilities don't separate classes confidently enough to ever reach the risk bands docs/decision-policy.md § 5 defines, on this sample. The mechanism is real and unit-tested (tests/unit/test_action_risk.py, tests/unit/test_authorization.py) with a manufactured score; it simply has zero measured effect here given this model's actual score distribution — reported honestly, not hidden.
